title: Your first power chord
summary: Sound a root and its fifth together.

steps.title: Your first power chord
steps.body:
**power chord** means a root and a perfect 5th sounding together, sometimes with the root repeated an octave higher. G5 means a G power chord: G and D. The 5 names the distance, not five different notes. Without the middle note of a triad, this chord is neither major nor minor.

**Why it matters:** Two note names give you a small, movable chord sound to learn.

steps.title: Read the positions
steps.body: For G5, use string 6 fret 3, string 5 fret 5 and string 4 fret 5. Leave strings 3, 2 and 1 out. The notes are G2, D3 and G3: the two G sounds repeat the root.

items.prompt: Play G and D together. Use any positions for these notes.

steps.title: Make it comfortable
steps.body: First sound just G and D, then add the higher G. The app accepts either version because there are still only two different note names. Use tap input for the chord check; the microphone hears one note at a time.

items.prompt: How far apart are these two notes?
Play G and D together. Use any positions for these notes.
